name: Half Guard to Jailbreak
description: Enter the 10th Planet Jailbreak from bottom half guard. Secure the underhook, turn into the inversion, and convert crushing top pressure into an explosive escape junction.
summary: Half Guard to Jailbreak is a 10th Planet entry in which the bottom half guard player secures a same-side underhook and turns into an inverted setup, converting the top player's forward crossface pressure into the Jailbreak escape junction.
overview:
Half Guard to Jailbreak is the entry that lands a flattened bottom half guard player into the Jailbreak position, the dynamic 10th Planet escape junction. Rather than grinding for a traditional knee-shield or frame recovery, the bottom player accepts the top player's forward pressure as fuel: they win or maintain the same-side underhook, tuck the chin, and turn their shoulders toward the trapped-leg side to load the explosive inversion.

The entry is fundamentally a baiting and timing exchange. A skilled passer wants to flatten the half guard bottom player with a heavy crossface and drive their weight forward to complete the pass. The Jailbreak entry uses that exact forward commitment - the moment the passer's center of gravity advances over a narrow base is the moment the underhook-and-invert becomes mechanically viable. The bottom player is not trying to sweep or recover guard in this single action; they are arriving at the Jailbreak junction from which the explosive roll, deep half dive, or back take then unfolds.

Because it trades the relative safety of a framed half guard for a committed, dynamic position, the entry carries real risk: if the underhook is lost or the timing is early, the passer can flatten the bottom player completely and finish the pass to side control. Executed against forward pressure with a tight underhook and tucked chin, however, it is one of the most reliable ways for a modern no-gi guard player to turn a losing flattened half guard into an active offensive scramble.
conditions: Bottom player is in bottom half guard, typically already flattened or being flattened by top pressure
Bottom player has secured or can win the same-side underhook (same side as the trapped leg)
Top player is committing weight forward with crossface, shoulder, or chest pressure
Bottom player has enough flexibility and neck safety to tuck the chin and begin inverting

attacker.name: Half Guard to Jailbreak Attacker
attacker.description: How to enter the Jailbreak from bottom half guard. Underhook timing, chin tuck, inversion load, and the chain into the explosive 10th Planet escape junction.
attacker.overview:
As the attacker entering Half Guard to Jailbreak, you are the bottom half guard player turning a defensive, flattened position into an offensive junction. Your job in this single transition is not to finish a sweep or fully recover guard - it is to arrive cleanly at the Jailbreak position with your underhook intact and your inversion loaded. Everything downstream (the explosive roll to turtle, the back take, the deep half dive) depends on getting this entry right.

The entry hinges on two things: winning the same-side underhook and reading your opponent's forward pressure. When the passer commits their weight forward to flatten and pass you, their base narrows and their center of gravity advances - this is precisely the moment you turn into them, tuck your chin, and begin to invert. You are converting their pressure into your rotational momentum rather than fighting it head-on.

This is a high-reward, medium-risk action characteristic of the 10th Planet half guard game. Done with a tight underhook and correct timing, you land in a dynamic position with multiple offensive paths. Done with a loose underhook or premature timing, you hand the passer the flattening angle they wanted and risk being passed straight to side control. Commitment and connection are everything.
key_principles: Win and keep the same-side underhook - it is the structural fulcrum that lets you arrive at the Jailbreak with control rather than getting flattened
Use the passer's forward pressure as fuel: enter when their weight commits over a narrow base, not when they are sitting back and based wide
Tuck the chin and round the shoulders before inverting to protect the neck and enable a smooth granby-style turn
Turn toward your trapped-leg side so your hips and shoulders rotate as a connected unit into the inversion
Stay connected with elbow-to-hip on the underhook side so the passer cannot peel you off as you turn
Treat this as an arrival, not a finish - your goal is to reach the Jailbreak junction loaded, then choose roll, back take, or deep half
setup_requirements: Bottom half guard established, even if flattened, with at least one leg trapping the opponent's leg
Same-side underhook secured or actively being won, with the elbow drawn tight to your own hip
Recognition that the top player is driving weight forward with crossface or shoulder pressure rather than sitting back
Free leg posted on the mat or framing on the opponent's hip to generate rotation and prevent being fully flattened
Chin tucked and neck braced so the inversion does not load the cervical spine
Enough hip space to begin turning toward the trapped-leg side without being completely chest-pinned

execution_steps.description: From bottom half guard, drive your underhook arm deep under the opponent's same-side armpit (the side of your trapped leg) and pull your elbow tight to your own hip. This connection is the lifeline of the entry - without it, turning in just exposes your back and neck. Fight to re-pummel it if the passer strips it.

execution_steps.action: Bait or read the forward pressure
execution_steps.description: Invite the passer to commit by giving them a flatter-looking target, or simply read the moment they drive their crossface and shoulder forward to finish the pass. The entry only works when their weight is forward over a narrow base, so wait for that commitment rather than forcing the turn against a wide, seated base.

execution_steps.action: Tuck the chin and round the shoulders
execution_steps.description: As you feel the forward weight, tuck your chin hard toward your chest and round your upper back. This protects your neck for the coming inversion and pre-loads the granby-style rolling shape. Look toward your own belt rather than up at your opponent to keep the spine safe.

Rotate your hips and shoulders together toward the side of your trapped leg, keeping the underhook elbow glued to your hip. This is the turn that points you into the Jailbreak. The motion should feel like you are corkscrewing under the opponent's pressure rather than pushing away from it.

execution_steps.action: Post the free leg and load the inversion
execution_steps.description: Drive your free (non-trapped) foot into the mat and use it to push your hips up and over, beginning to invert your shoulders toward the mat. The free leg supplies the propulsion that turns a static turn into a loaded inversion, and frames the opponent's hip so they cannot simply re-flatten you.

With the underhook held, chin tucked, and shoulders inverting, you have now reached the Jailbreak position - hips turned, free leg active, and the explosive roll loaded. Pause your decision here only as long as needed to read the opponent: continue the roll to turtle, chain to a back take if they follow, or dive to deep half if they base wide.

common_counters.counter: Passer strips your underhook before you turn, then drives the crossface to flatten you
common_counters.your_response: Abort the inversion the instant the underhook is gone. Re-pummel for the underhook or build a knee shield and frame to recover standard half guard rather than turning in blind, which would feed your back and neck.

common_counters.counter: Passer sits back and bases wide with hips down, refusing to commit weight forward
common_counters.your_response: Do not force the Jailbreak turn into a wide defensive base. Switch to a deep half dive under their hips, or threaten an old school sweep on the underhook to draw their weight forward before re-attempting the entry.

common_counters.counter: Passer follows your inversion roll, chasing to maintain top control
common_counters.your_response: Welcome it - if they chase the roll, keep the underhook and continue the momentum into a back take rather than stopping. Their follow exposes their back to your underhook-driven rotation.

common_errors.error: Turning in without first securing the underhook
common_errors.consequence: You expose your back and neck; the passer takes the back or flattens you straight to side control.
common_errors.correction: Always win and glue the same-side underhook (elbow to hip) before you begin the turn. No underhook, no Jailbreak entry.

common_errors.error: Entering against a wide, seated passing base
common_errors.consequence: There is no forward weight to convert into rotation, so the turn stalls and you get smashed flat.
common_errors.correction: Wait for, or bait, the passer's forward weight commitment. If they stay based wide, switch to deep half instead of forcing the Jailbreak.

common_errors.error: Failing to tuck the chin during the inversion
common_errors.consequence: The roll loads your cervical spine, risking neck injury and stalling the motion mid-turn.
common_errors.correction: Tuck the chin to your chest and look at your own belt before and during the turn. Protect the neck first, then invert.

common_errors.error: Leaving the free leg passive instead of posting and driving
common_errors.consequence: Without propulsion the inversion is sluggish, giving the passer time to re-flatten and kill the entry.
common_errors.correction: Post the free foot firmly and drive your hips up and over with it to power a sharp, committed inversion.

common_errors.error: Hesitating at the halfway point of the turn
common_errors.consequence: A half-committed turn is the worst of both worlds - you give up your frames without arriving at the Jailbreak, and the passer flattens you.
common_errors.correction: Once you commit to the turn, follow it all the way to the Jailbreak junction. Decide before you turn, then execute decisively.

training_progressions.focus: Securing the same-side underhook and the basic turn-in shape
training_progressions.description: With a compliant partner holding light top half guard pressure, drill winning the underhook (elbow to hip) and turning toward the trapped-leg side with chin tucked. No explosive inversion yet - focus on the connection and the direction of the turn. 15-20 reps per side.

training_progressions.focus: Reading and using the passer's forward weight
training_progressions.description: Partner alternates between driving forward and basing wide. You enter the Jailbreak turn only when they commit weight forward, and switch to a deep half dive when they base wide. Develops the core timing read of the entry. 6-8 minutes of reactive drilling.

training_progressions.focus: Adding free-leg propulsion and full inversion to the junction
training_progressions.description: Partner applies medium crossface pressure. Add the free-leg post and drive to load the inversion and arrive at the full Jailbreak position. Chain one follow-up (roll to turtle) each rep so the entry connects to an outcome. 10-12 reps per side.

training_progressions.focus: Entering the Jailbreak under resistance from live half guard
training_progressions.description: Start in bottom half guard with a resisting passer working to flatten and pass. Score by cleanly reaching the Jailbreak junction with the underhook intact, then continue into roll, back take, or deep half. 4-5 minute rounds, increasing resistance.

flashcards.question: What single control point must you secure before turning into the Jailbreak from half guard?
flashcards.answer: The same-side underhook - the underhook on the same side as your trapped leg, with the elbow drawn tight to your own hip. It is the structural fulcrum that lets you turn in without exposing your back or neck, and it keeps you connected to the opponent so they cannot peel you off as you invert. Turning in without it feeds your back and leads straight to being passed.

flashcards.question: Why is the passer's forward pressure an advantage rather than a problem for this entry?
flashcards.answer: When the passer drives their weight forward to flatten and pass you, their base narrows and their center of gravity advances over you. That forward commitment is exactly the energy you convert into rotational momentum for the inversion. Instead of fighting the pressure head-on, you turn into it and corkscrew under it, so a heavier forward drive actually makes the Jailbreak entry more available, not less.

flashcards.question: How do you decide between entering the Jailbreak versus diving to deep half?
flashcards.answer: Read the passer's base and weight. If they commit their weight forward over a narrow base, the Jailbreak turn-and-invert is viable because there is forward energy to redirect. If they sit back and base wide with their hips down, there is no forward weight to convert, so you dive underneath them to deep half instead. Both options use the same same-side underhook as the entry point - the passer's pressure dictates which you choose.

flashcards.question: What protects your neck during the inversion, and where should your eyes go?
flashcards.answer: Tucking your chin hard to your chest and rounding your upper back protects the cervical spine and creates the granby-style rolling shape needed for a smooth turn. Your eyes should look toward your own belt rather than up at the opponent. Keeping the chin tucked throughout the turn is non-negotiable; failing to do so loads the neck and stalls the inversion.

flashcards.question: Your turn is only halfway done and you feel yourself stalling - what went wrong and what do you do?
flashcards.answer: Hesitation at the halfway point is the most dangerous failure: you have given up your half guard frames without arriving at the Jailbreak, so the passer can flatten you to side control. The fix is to commit fully once you begin the turn - drive the free leg and finish all the way to the junction. The deeper lesson is to make the decision before you turn so you never enter half-committed.

attacker.safety_considerations: This entry involves an inverting, granby-style rotation, so neck safety is the foremost concern. The chin must be tucked to the chest and the load carried on the rounded upper back and shoulders, never on the crown of the head or an extended neck. Beginners should build the inversion gradually with a compliant partner before adding explosive speed or resistance, and should never force the turn if the neck feels compressed. Both partners should communicate during drilling, and the bottom player should abort the inversion if the underhook is lost rather than rolling through blind.

defender.name: Half Guard to Jailbreak Defender
defender.description: How to defend against the Jailbreak entry from top half guard. Recognize the underhook turn, deny forward weight, and pass to side control before the inversion loads.
defender.overview:
As the defender against Half Guard to Jailbreak, you are the top half guard player trying to flatten and pass while your opponent attempts to convert your pressure into an inverting escape. Your goal is to deny the entry before it loads - to flatten and pass straight to side control, or to strip the underhook so the turn-in exposes your opponent's back instead of escaping yours.

The key tension is that your own forward pressure is what feeds the Jailbreak. A reckless, over-committed weight drive over a narrow base gives the bottom player the exact rotational energy they want. The skilled defense is to apply pressure with a wide, heavy base, control the underhook side, and pass through angles that do not hand them the inversion. When you feel them tuck the chin and turn toward their trapped leg, you must immediately choose: kill the underhook and chase the back, or widen your base and switch your hips to deny the roll.

The highest-percentage defense prevents the entry entirely by stripping or limping-arm-ing the underhook before they can connect elbow to hip. Once the inversion is loaded, your window narrows quickly, and chasing the roll without a plan can hand them a back take. Read the underhook battle early and you control the entire exchange.
key_principles: Control or strip the same-side underhook early - without it the bottom player cannot safely turn into the Jailbreak
Pass with a wide, heavy base; do not over-commit weight forward over a narrow base that feeds their rotation
Recognize the chin tuck and turn-toward-trapped-leg as the entry signal and react before the inversion loads
When they turn in, threaten their exposed back rather than passively following the roll
Switch your hips and widen your base to deny the rolling momentum if you cannot strip the underhook in time
Prioritize completing the pass to side control over chasing a low-percentage submission as they turn
recognition_cues: The bottom player digs hard for a deep same-side underhook and pulls their elbow tight to their own hip
The bottom player tucks their chin to their chest and rounds their shoulders rather than framing to push you away
The bottom player begins rotating their hips and shoulders toward their trapped-leg side as you drive forward
You feel your forward weight suddenly being absorbed and redirected into a turning, corkscrewing motion beneath you

defensive_options.action: Strip or limp-arm the underhook and re-flatten before they can turn
defensive_options.when_to_use: Earliest recognition - when they are still digging for or have just won the underhook but have not yet tucked and turned
defensive_options.if_successful: Without the underhook their turn-in exposes the back and you flatten them, completing the pass to side control
defensive_options.risk: Committing both hands to the underhook fight can momentarily free their frames if you mistime it

defensive_options.action: Widen your base and switch your hips to deny the rolling momentum
defensive_options.when_to_use: Mid-entry - when they have begun the turn and you cannot strip the underhook in time
defensive_options.if_successful: Your wide base absorbs the rotation, the inversion stalls, and they are forced back to a flat half guard with no escape
defensive_options.risk: If you widen too late or lift your hips, you may feed the roll and hand them the Jailbreak junction

defensive_options.action: Follow the turn to chase their exposed back
defensive_options.when_to_use: When they fully commit to the inversion and their back briefly turns toward you
defensive_options.if_successful: You ride the rotation, hunt for hooks or a seatbelt, and turn their escape attempt into your back-control opportunity
defensive_options.risk: An undisciplined chase can be reversed - if they keep the underhook they may take your back instead as you follow

favorable_outcomes.how: Strip or neutralize the underhook early, keep a wide heavy base so your forward pressure is not converted into their rotation, and drive your chest and crossface through to flatten them. With the underhook gone and their turn killed, complete the pass to side control.

If you cannot strip the underhook in time, widen your base and switch your hips to absorb the inversion. The roll stalls and they are forced back to a flat, controlled half guard rather than reaching the Jailbreak junction.

common_errors.error: Driving your weight forward over a narrow base to flatten them
common_errors.consequence: Your forward commitment is exactly the rotational energy the Jailbreak feeds on; they corkscrew under you and reach the junction.
common_errors.correction: Apply pressure with a wide, heavy base and your hips down. Make your weight hard to redirect rather than charging forward over a narrow stance.

common_errors.error: Ignoring the underhook battle until they have already connected elbow to hip
common_errors.consequence: Once the underhook is glued in, the safe turn-in is available and your window to deny the entry has largely closed.
common_errors.correction: Fight the underhook early and continuously. Strip, limp-arm, or pin the underhooking arm before they can seat the elbow to their hip.

common_errors.error: Passively following the inversion roll without a plan
common_errors.consequence: Chasing the roll while they keep the underhook lets them continue the momentum into a back take on you.
common_errors.correction: Only follow the turn if you are actively hunting their exposed back; otherwise widen your base and stall the roll instead of chasing.

flashcards.question: Why can your own forward pressure work against you when defending the Jailbreak entry?
flashcards.answer: The Jailbreak entry converts your forward weight into the bottom player's rotational momentum. If you over-commit your weight forward over a narrow base, you hand them exactly the energy they need to corkscrew under you and load the inversion. The defensive correction is to pressure with a wide, heavy base and your hips down so your weight is hard to redirect rather than charging forward where it feeds their turn.

flashcards.question: What is the single most effective way to prevent the Jailbreak entry before it starts?
flashcards.answer: Win the underhook battle early. The bottom player needs the same-side underhook with their elbow glued to their hip to turn in safely. If you strip it, limp-arm it, or pin the underhooking arm before they connect, their turn-in exposes their own back instead of escaping, and you can flatten and pass to side control. Neglecting the underhook fight until it is seated is what gives them the entry.

flashcards.question: They have already begun the inversion and you cannot strip the underhook - what do you do?
flashcards.answer: Widen your base and switch your hips to absorb the rolling momentum rather than chasing the roll blindly. A wide base stalls the inversion and forces them back to a flat half guard. Only follow the turn if you are actively hunting their exposed back; an undisciplined chase while they keep the underhook can let them take your back instead.

training_progressions.focus: Recognizing the underhook, chin tuck, and turn-in cues
training_progressions.description: Partner telegraphs the Jailbreak entry slowly from bottom half guard. Practice spotting the same-side underhook, the chin tuck, and the turn toward the trapped leg, and verbally call the cue before reacting. Builds early recognition. 15-20 reps.

training_progressions.focus: Stripping and limping the underhook before it seats
training_progressions.description: Partner repeatedly digs for the underhook at medium intensity. Drill stripping, limp-arming, and re-flattening before they connect elbow to hip, completing the pass toward side control. 10-12 reps per side.

training_progressions.focus: Denying the Jailbreak under resistance and passing
training_progressions.description: Start in top half guard with the bottom player actively hunting the Jailbreak entry. Defend by controlling the underhook and base width, and score by passing to side control or stalling them flat. 4-5 minute rounds with increasing resistance.

variants_and_adaptations.description: When already fully flattened with a heavy crossface, win the underhook deeper and use the passer's maximum forward pressure as the trigger, turning immediately into the inversion before they can finish the crossface pass. The most desperate but highest-energy-return version of the entry.
variants_and_adaptations.when_to_use: When you have already been flattened and standard frame recovery is no longer available

variants_and_adaptations.description: Threaten the old school sweep on the underhook to draw the passer's weight forward; when they post wide to defend the sweep and commit forward, transition the same underhook into the Jailbreak turn instead.
variants_and_adaptations.when_to_use: Against a passer who bases wide to defend the underhook sweep, drawing their weight forward enough to enter the inversion

position_integration: Half Guard to Jailbreak is the primary on-ramp into the 10th Planet Jailbreak escape system from one of grappling's most common losing spots - flattened bottom half guard. It sits at the junction of the underhook half guard game: the same same-side underhook that drives the old school sweep and the deep half dive also powers this entry, and the passer's response (forward weight versus wide base) determines which of those paths opens. Strategically, the entry reframes a defensive crisis as an offensive scramble, connecting the static half guard battle to the dynamic Jailbreak outcomes of roll-to-turtle, back take, and deep half. Mastering it gives the bottom player a reliable answer to heavy pressure passing in modern no-gi, where flattened half guard would otherwise lead directly to a pass.
